action_items: OPTIONAL — Suppress the '<span> cannot be a child of <select>' hydration warning on Hero3D (homepage): the Emergent visual-editor auto-wrapping of <option> elements inside <select> is not compatible with React 18 hydration. Could be filtered via a small ve-editor guard, or by refactoring the month picker to a custom (non-native) dropdown. Not a bug — cosmetic console noise.

OPTIONAL — Consider increasing the GET /api/pack-karmique/status and GET /api/rencontres/ultime/status HTTP response speed: some polls take 15-30s to respond during heavy background PDF generation (I had to bump my test client timeout from 15s to 45s to avoid ReadTimeout). Could hint at Supabase table select or event loop contention while pack_karmique / rencontres_ultime pipelines are running. Not blocking end-users (page polls every 3.5s in the UI).
critical_code_review_comments: pack_karmique.py checkout enforces email + birth_date + birth_time but not first_name — the frontend enforces first_name client-side. If someone hits the API directly with an empty first_name, the PDF will still be generated with an empty/placeholder name. Not a bug per se but worth mirroring the client validation server-side for consistency.
rencontres.py checkout raises HTTPException(400, 'Le prénom de la personne qui t'intéresse est requis.') — correctly French and specific. Nice.
The Starfield component (39 lines) is well isolated and mounted once in App.js at line 74 — the useMemo prevents re-computation. LGTM.
Homepage still exhibits hydration warnings inherited from iteration_46 (Emergent visual editor <span> injection inside <select>). Non-critical but should be addressed one day.

rca_of_the_issue: No critical bug found. The only observation worth logging: /api/pack-karmique/status and /api/rencontres/ultime/status may occasionally exceed 15s response time while a heavy PDF generation is running in-process — the FastAPI event loop is briefly starved by the sync Supabase client / PDF rendering. In practice the frontend polls every 3.5s with default axios timeout and it works, but under load it could be worth (a) moving the Supabase status query behind a thread executor, or (b) capping PDF generation concurrency. Not a bug fix required now.
